newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ECONOMISTS' COMMENTS ON DUTCH CPB FORECASTS.
newsitem.headline: ECONOMISTS' COMMENTS ON DUTCH CPB FORECASTS.

text.p: The Dutch government's Central Planning Bureau (CPB) published a new set of forecasts for the Dutch economy on Thursday.
The CPB said it expected gross domestic product to grow by 3.0 percent in 1997 and 3.25 percent in 1998. It forecast inflation rates of 2.75 percent in 1997 and 2.0 percent in 1998.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on the CPB forecasts:

ALINE SCHUILING, MEESPIERSON: "I think the CPB inflation estimate for 1998 (2.0 pct) is too low. That's very unlikely because there has been increased pressure from wages rises lately...I'm looking for inflation of around 2.5 percent this year and 2.75 percent next year...We agree with the CPB that there will be a slowdown in growth of consumer spending and an acceleration of exports...but I see slightly slower export growth than the CPB in 1997 because we're only moderately optimistic about the outlook for Germany and France this year... I expect Dutch GDP growth of 2.5/2.75 pct in 1997 and around 3.0 pct in 1998."

PAUL VAN DE VEN, RABOBANK NEDERLAND: "The GDP forecasts are completely in line with our forecasts. It's the export sector that will take over from consumer spending in driving GDP. The CPB is saying the Dutch economy is in good shape. All factors show there's a lot of confidence among consumers and producers...the Netherlands' competitiveness is strong...The CPB expects quite a substantial decline in the dollar (to around 1.80 guilders from 1.88 now). We think that will occur mostly in 1998. But their inflation forecast of 2.0 percent in 1998 could turn out to be a little on the low side."

LEO KRANENBURG, GENERALE BANK: "The forecasts for this year are reasonably in line with our own. For 1998 I think they're a bit too optimistic with an overall growth estimate of 3.25 percent. We think 3.0 percent GDP growth in 1997 could well be the peak. We expect overall growth to decline to 2.5 pct in 1998 with slightly less exuberant export growth... We have our doubts about the power of the recovery in Europe, also bearing in mind the ups and downs of EMU...We wouldn't argue with their inflation forecast for 1997 but we think that a fall to 2.0 percent next year is a bit optimistic. We expect 2.75 pct...We see the dollar at 1.90 guilders in 1997, a bit lower in 1998."
